title: Grammatical Gender and Basic Nominative Plurals
subtitle: Recognize noun genders by endings and form basic plurals in Slovak
keyPoint: Slovak nouns belong to one of three genders—masculine (usually ending in a consonant), feminine (ending in -a), or neuter (ending in -o, -e, or -ie)—and each forms plurals with specific vowel suffixes.

useCases.label: Masculine Noun Plurals
useCases.example: Títo noví študenti čítajú knihy.

useCases.label: Feminine Noun Plurals
useCases.example: Na stole ležia staré mapy.

useCases.label: Neuter Noun Plurals
useCases.example: Moderné mestá sú veľmi pekné.

examples.en: Na dvore brešú veľkí psi.
V izbe sú nové stoly.
Moje sestry študujú v Bratislave.
Tieto zelené jablká sú sladké.
V knižnici sú zaujímavé knihy.

mistakes.note: Neuter and feminine nouns use the numeral 'dve', whereas 'dva' is only for masculine nouns.
Nominative plural feminine adjectives end in -é, not -ý.
Inanimate masculine nouns ending in a hard consonant take -y, not -i.

quiz.question: Choose the correct plural form for 'kniha' (book):
quiz.explanation: Feminine nouns ending in -a preceded by a hard consonant take the plural ending -y.

quiz.question: Which of these nouns is neuter?
quiz.explanation: Nouns ending in -o (like okno) are neuter in Slovak.

quiz.question: Choose the correct plural: 'V parku behajú ___.' (boys)
quiz.explanation: Masculine animate nouns typically end in -i in the nominative plural, causing 'k' to soften to 'c' (chlapec → chlapci).

quiz.question: What is the nominative plural of 'auto' (car)?
quiz.explanation: Neuter nouns ending in -o replace it with -á in the plural (auto → autá).

tip: Look at the last letter of a Slovak noun in nominative singular: a consonant usually means masculine, -a means feminine, and -o or -e means neuter.

title: Present Tense Conjugation Classes
subtitle: Master the primary present tense verb patterns and subject-pronoun dropping
keyPoint: Slovak verbs conjugate in the present tense by attaching person-specific endings to stem classes (-á, -í, -ie, -e), allowing subject pronouns to be dropped routinely.

useCases.label: Habitual or Daily Action
useCases.example: Každé ráno pijem čierny čaj.

useCases.label: Current State or Action
useCases.example: Teraz píšeme dôležitú úlohu.

useCases.label: Dropped Pronouns in Dialogue
useCases.example: Hovoríš po slovensky?

examples.en: Každý deň čítam noviny.
Čo robíte cez víkend?
Oni nerozumejú po anglicky.
Bývame v malom byte.
Peter píše dlhý list rodine.

mistakes.wrong: Ja som študent a ja bývam tu.
mistakes.note: Slovak is a pro-drop language; repeating 'ja' sounds unnatural unless emphasizing contrast.
Third-person plural never ends in -ť; -ť is the infinitive marker.
The 1st person plural ending is -me, while -te is for 2nd person plural.

quiz.question: Complete the sentence: 'My ___ po slovensky.' (hovoriť - we speak)
quiz.explanation: The 1st person plural ('my') ending for the -í conjugation is -íme (hovoríme).

quiz.question: Complete the sentence: 'Peter ___ novú prácu.' (hľadať - Peter searches)
quiz.explanation: Peter is 3rd person singular ('on'), taking the ending -á for the -á class.

quiz.question: Which form matches 'oni' for the verb 'pracovať' (to work)?
quiz.explanation: Verbs ending in -ovať conjugate as -ujem, -uješ... -ujú in 3rd person plural.

quiz.question: Complete the sentence: 'Čo ___ ty dnes večer?' (robiť - you do)
quiz.explanation: The 2nd person singular ('ty') takes the ending -š (robíš).

tip: Since verb endings clearly identify who is performing the action, omit subject pronouns like 'ja' or 'ty' unless you need contrast or emphasis.

title: Accusative Case and Masculine Animacy
subtitle: Direct objects and the essential animate vs. inanimate masculine contrast
keyPoint: In the accusative case, feminine nouns change -a to -u, neuters and inanimate masculines remain identical to the nominative, but masculine animate nouns take the genitive ending -a.

useCases.label: Direct Object with Person or Pet
useCases.example: Čakám na svojho brata.

useCases.label: Direct Object with Inanimate Thing
useCases.example: Kupujem nový stôl.

useCases.label: Direct Object with Feminine Noun
useCases.example: Dám si jednu kávu.

examples.en: Poznám tvojho dobrého otca.
Vidím vysoký moderný dom.
Mám rád horúcu polievku.
Hľadáte nášho psa?
Pijem studené mlieko.

mistakes.note: Masculine animate direct objects must take the accusative ending -a (matching the genitive).
'Stôl' is masculine inanimate, so it keeps nominative form and requires masculine agreement.
Feminine nouns ending in -a must change to -u when used as direct objects.

quiz.question: Complete the sentence: 'Poznáš toho nového ___?' (učiteľ - teacher)
quiz.explanation: Učiteľ is masculine animate, so its accusative singular ending is -a (učiteľa).

quiz.question: Complete the sentence: 'Čítam zaujímavú ___.' (kniha - book)
quiz.explanation: Feminine nouns ending in -a shift to -u in the accusative case.

quiz.question: Complete the sentence: 'Kupujem tento ___.' (telefón - phone)
quiz.explanation: Telefón is masculine inanimate, so accusative is identical to nominative.

quiz.question: Which accusative phrase is grammatically correct for 'I see a good friend' (male friend)?
quiz.explanation: Masculine animate adjectives take -ého and nouns take -a in the accusative.

tip: Ask 'Koho? Čo?' (Whom or What?) to test for the accusative: if it's a person/animal (Koho?), masculine nouns need -a; if it's an object (Čo?), masculine nouns don't change.

title: Locative Case with Static Prepositions
subtitle: Express static locations and topics using 'v', 'na', and 'o'
keyPoint: The locative case in Slovak is never used on its own; it always follows prepositions like 'v' (in), 'na' (on/at), or 'o' (about) to denote location or topic.

useCases.label: Enclosed Physical Location
useCases.example: Bývame v novom byte.

useCases.label: Surface or Event Location
useCases.example: Sme na koncerte v Bratislave.

useCases.label: Topic of Conversation/Thought
useCases.example: Rozprávame sa o politike.

examples.en: Pracujem v modernej kancelárii.
Kniha leží na drevenom stole.
Často rozmýšľam o budúcnosti.
Stretneme sa na pošte.
Deti sú teraz v škole.

mistakes.note: Slovakia takes the preposition 'na' and irregular locative ending -u (na Slovensku), not 'v'.
Locative requires an ending change; neuter nouns in -o take -e in the locative singular.
The preposition 'o' demands the locative case, requiring the -e ending for masculine inanimate nouns.

quiz.question: Complete the sentence: 'Bývam v ___.' (Bratislava)
quiz.explanation: Feminine hard-stem nouns take the ending -e in the locative singular after 'v'.

quiz.question: Which preposition is used for location with 'Slovensko'?
quiz.explanation: Countries usually take 'v', but Slovakia idiomatically takes 'na' (na Slovensku).

quiz.question: Complete the sentence: 'Kľúče sú na ___.' (stôl - table)
quiz.explanation: Masculine inanimate noun 'stôl' takes the locative ending -e (na stole).

quiz.question: Complete the sentence: 'Rozprávajú sa o novom ___.' (film - movie)
quiz.explanation: The preposition 'o' governs the locative case, producing 'o novom filme'.

tip: Remember that countries normally take 'v' (v Nemecku, v Rakúsku), but 'Slovensko' is an exception requiring 'na' (na Slovensku).

title: Past Tense and the 'l'-Participle
subtitle: Construct past tense actions using -l participles with 'byť' auxiliaries
keyPoint: The Slovak past tense combines the gender-marked 'l'-participle of the verb with the present-tense auxiliary of 'byť' in the 1st and 2nd persons, while dropping the auxiliary entirely in the 3rd person.

useCases.label: Personal Past Experience
useCases.example: Včera som bol v kine.

useCases.label: Completed Action by Third Person
useCases.example: Mama varila obed.

useCases.label: Inquiring About Past Events
useCases.example: Kde si bol cez víkend?

examples.en: Včera som čítal zaujímavú knihu.
Kde ste kúpili to auto?
Zuzana nebola včera v škole.
My sme bývali v Košiciach päť rokov.
Oni prišli domov veľmi neskoro.

mistakes.note: Never use the auxiliary verb 'je' or 'sú' in the 3rd person past tense.
The gender of the l-participle, predicate adjective, and speaker must agree (feminine -a).
The auxiliary 'sme' is a clitic and naturally sits in second position, not attached clumsily at the end.

quiz.question: How does a female speaker say 'I worked'?
quiz.explanation: A female speaker uses the feminine past participle suffix -la with the 1st person singular auxiliary 'som'.

quiz.question: Complete the 3rd person sentence: 'Peter včera ___ futbal.' (hrať)
quiz.explanation: Third-person past tense requires no auxiliary verb; just the masculine participle 'hral'.

quiz.question: Complete the sentence: 'Čo ste včera ___?' (vy / robiť - plural)
quiz.explanation: Plural past participles always take the ending -li (robili).

quiz.question: Where does the auxiliary 'si' belong in: 'Kde ___ včera večer?' (ty / byť)
quiz.explanation: The auxiliary 'si' occupies the second grammatical position: 'Kde si bol včera večer?'

tip: Third person forms NEVER take an auxiliary: say 'on robil' or 'ona písala', never add 'je'!

title: Modal Verbs and Prefixed Negation
subtitle: Expressing ability, necessity, desire, and knowledge with prefixed 'ne-'
keyPoint: Slovak modal verbs are followed by an infinitive, and verbs are negated directly by attaching the prefix 'ne-' directly to the conjugated verb.

useCases.label: Expressing Necessity
useCases.example: Dnes musím pracovať dlho do večera.

useCases.label: Expressing Inability or Refusal
useCases.example: Bohužiaľ nemôžem prísť na tvoju oslavu.

useCases.label: Acquired Skills and Knowledge
useCases.example: Vieš hovoriť po slovensky veľmi dobre.

examples.en: Dnes večer nechcem variť večeru.
Môžem si tu sadnúť?
Zajtra musíme vstávať veľmi skoro ráno.
Môj brat nevie plávať v hlbokej vode.
Tento týždeň nemusíte písať domáce úlohy.

mistakes.note: Negation in Slovak is a bound prefix attached directly to the verb ('nechcem'), not a detached word ('nie chcem').
A modal verb must be followed by an infinitive (-ť ending), never by a conjugated verb form.

mistakes.wrong: Ja viem plávať ale dnes neviem prísť.
mistakes.right: Ja viem plávať ale dnes nemôžem prísť.
mistakes.note: Use 'môcť' for circumstantial possibility/permission and 'vedieť' exclusively for learned skills or knowledge.

quiz.question: Peter ___ prísť na stretnutie, pretože má chrípku.
quiz.explanation: 'Nemôže' expresses the external physical impossibility of coming, and negation merges into the verb as 'ne-'.

quiz.question: Ospravedlňujem sa, ale ___ tvoje telefónne číslo.
quiz.explanation: The negative form of 'viem' (I know) is written as a single word: 'neviem'.

quiz.question: Deti, ___ rýchlo upratať svoje izby!
quiz.explanation: 'Musíte' (you must - plural) fits the imperative context of necessity followed by the infinitive 'upratať'.

quiz.question: Prepáčte, dnes naozaj ___ ísť do kina.
quiz.explanation: The 1st person singular ('I') form of chcieť negated is 'nechcem'.

tip: Remember that 'nemusieť' means 'don't have to' (absence of obligation), not 'must not'. For prohibition, Slovak uses 'nesmieť' (e.g., 'nesmieš' = you must not).

title: Verbal Aspect: Perfective vs. Imperfective
subtitle: Distinguishing between ongoing actions and completed results
keyPoint: Imperfective verbs focus on ongoing or repeated actions, while perfective verbs express completed actions with a clear result.

useCases.label: Ongoing Process (Imperfective)
useCases.example: Včera večer som písal list dve hodiny.

useCases.label: Single Completed Result (Perfective)
useCases.example: Už som napísal celú správu pre šéfa.

useCases.label: Regular Repeated Action (Imperfective)
useCases.example: Každé ráno kupujem čerstvé pečivo.

examples.en: Celé popoludnie čítala zaujímavú knihu.
Konečne prečítal celú učebnicu na skúšku.
Zajtra uvarím obed pre celú rodinu.
Mama varila obed, keď zazvonil telefón.
Vždy zatváram okná, keď odchádzam z domu.

mistakes.note: Perfective verbs form the future tense using their present tense conjugations alone; never combine 'budem' with a perfective infinitive.
Habitual or repeated daily actions require imperfective verbs ('čítal'), not perfective result verbs ('prečítal').
Duration expressions ('dve hodiny') require imperfective verbs because they describe the duration of a process.

quiz.question: Peter včera celý večer ___ na počítači novú hru.
quiz.explanation: 'Celý večer' indicates duration of a process, demanding the imperfective verb 'hral'.

quiz.question: Už si ___ tú novú knihu, ktorú som ti požičal?
quiz.explanation: 'Už' (already) asks about completion and result, requiring the perfective past form 'prečítal'.

quiz.question: Zajtra ti určite ___ všetky peniaze.
quiz.explanation: A single future completion takes the simple perfective present-future form 'vrátim'.

quiz.question: Každé ráno o siedmej ___ do práce električkou.
quiz.explanation: 'Každé ráno' describes a repeated habitual action, requiring the imperfective 'cestujem'.

tip: Perfective verbs do not have a compound future with 'budem'. The present tense forms of perfective verbs (e.g. urobím, kúpim, prečítam) automatically refer to future completed actions!

title: Genitive Case: Possession, Absence, and Numbers
subtitle: Expressing ownership, absence with 'niet', and counting from 5 onward
keyPoint: The genitive indicates possession, follows prepositions like 'od', 'do', and 'bez', and is required after numerals 5 and above as well as negated existence.

useCases.label: Possession (Whose?)
useCases.example: Toto je auto môjho staršieho brata.

useCases.label: Counting Quantities (5+)
useCases.example: Na námestí stojí päť vysokých stromov.

useCases.label: Absence with 'bez' or 'niet'
useCases.example: Kávu pijem vždy bez bieleho cukru.

examples.en: Dnes prišiel do školy bez domácej úlohy.
Kúpil som šesť zelených jabĺk v obchode.
Cestujeme od Bratislavy až do Košíc.
Tu niet žiadnej pomoci.
Kabát môjho otca visí v predsieni.

mistakes.note: Numbers from five upwards govern the genitive plural ('nových kamarátov'), not the nominative plural.
The preposition 'bez' (without) always triggers the genitive case ('brata').

mistakes.wrong: Kniha od môj učiteľ leží tu.
mistakes.right: Kniha od môjho učiteľa leží tu.
mistakes.note: Both adjective and noun must decline into the genitive singular after the preposition 'od'.

quiz.question: V kaviarni si objednal čaj bez ___.
quiz.explanation: The preposition 'bez' always governs the genitive case ('cukru').

quiz.question: Na parkovisku pred domom stojí sedem ___.
quiz.explanation: Numerals 5 and higher govern nouns and adjectives in the genitive plural ('nových áut').

quiz.question: Toto je taška mojej sestry a toto je kabát môjho ___.
quiz.explanation: Expressing possession ('of my father') requires the masculine animate genitive singular suffix '-a'.

quiz.question: Odchádzame na dovolenku od ___.
quiz.explanation: 'Od' governs the genitive case, turning 'pondelok' into 'pondelka'.

tip: Slovak feminine and neuter genitive plurals usually drop their final vowel and introduce a lengthening or diphthong inside the root (e.g., žena -> žien, mesto -> miest)!

title: Dative Case and Indirect Objects
subtitle: Identifying recipients, beneficiaries, and using prepositions 'k/ku' and 'proti'
keyPoint: The dative case answers 'to whom / for whom' (komu/čomu) an action is directed and is mandatory after prepositions like 'k/ku' (towards) and 'proti' (against).

useCases.label: Indirect Object (Recipient)
useCases.example: Otec kúpil malému synovi nový bicykel.

useCases.label: Direction Towards (k / ku)
useCases.example: Poobede ideme na návštevu k babke.

useCases.label: Opposition (proti)
useCases.example: Hráme dôležitý zápas proti rivalovi.

examples.en: Dal som kamarátovi kľúče od bytu.
Po práci idem rýchlo k lekárovi.
Táto masť pomáha proti bolesti hlavy.
Napíš svojej mame peknú správu.
Učiteľ vysvetľuje študentom novú gramatiku.

mistakes.note: The preposition 'k' requires the dative case. Masculine animate singular takes '-ovi'.
In Slovak, direct giving or sending takes the dative alone ('bratovi'), without using 'pre' (for).
The verb 'telefonovať' governs the dative case ('komu?'), not the accusative.

quiz.question: Peter podal ruku svojmu novému ___.
quiz.explanation: The recipient of an action takes dative masculine animate singular ending '-ovi'.

quiz.question: Zajtra pôjdeme na víkend ku ___.
quiz.explanation: The preposition 'ku' requires the dative plural: 'starým rodičom'.

quiz.question: Všetci občania bojujú proti ___.
quiz.explanation: The preposition 'proti' (against) takes dative singular ('nespravodlivosti').

quiz.question: Čo povieš svojej ___ o našom pláne?
quiz.explanation: Feminine dative singular takes the '-e' ending ('kamarátke').

tip: The preposition 'k' vocalizes into 'ku' before words starting with velar sounds /k/ or /g/, or clusters containing them (e.g., 'ku kapele', 'ku mne').

title: Instrumental Case: Means, Transport, and 's/so'
subtitle: Mastering instruments, transportation without prepositions, and accompaniment with 's/so'
keyPoint: Use the instrumental without a preposition for instruments and means of transport, but include the preposition 's/so' to express accompaniment ('with').

useCases.label: Accompaniment ('with')
useCases.example: Cestujem na dovolenku s mojou rodinou.

useCases.label: Means of Transport (no prep)
useCases.example: Do práce chodím každé ráno vlakom.

useCases.label: Tool or Instrument (no prep)
useCases.example: Píšem dôležitú zmluvu modrým perom.

examples.en: Rád jem polievku veľkou lyžicou.
Išiel do mesta autom, nie autobusom.
Pôjdeš dnes večer do kina so mnou?
Krájal chlieb ostrým nožom.
Učiteľka prišla na výlet so svojimi žiakmi.

mistakes.note: Means of transport do not take the preposition 's'. Using 's vlakom' implies you are accompanying the train as a companion.
Instruments used to perform an action take the bare instrumental without the preposition 's'.
The preposition 's' requires both adjective and noun in the instrumental case ('-ou' ending for feminine singular).

quiz.question: Do školy zvyčajne cestujeme mestským ___.
quiz.explanation: Means of transport take the bare instrumental without prepositions ('autobusom').

quiz.question: Bol si včera večer vonku so ___?
quiz.explanation: Accompaniment with 'so' requires the feminine instrumental ending '-ou': 'svojou sestrou'.

quiz.question: Tento list musíte podpísať čiernym ___.
quiz.explanation: Instruments or tools used to execute an action take the bare instrumental: 'čiernym perom'.

quiz.question: Chceš ísť dnes na obed so ___?
quiz.explanation: The 1st person singular pronoun after 'so' in the instrumental is 'mnou'.

tip: The preposition 's' vocalizes to 'so' whenever the following word begins with s, š, z, or ž (e.g., 'so sestrou', 'so ženou', 'so psom' due to cluster voicing).

title: Wackernagel's Law and Clitic Pronoun Placement
subtitle: Mastering the strict sequence of unstressed particles in the second position
keyPoint: Clitics are unaccented words that cluster together strictly in the clause's second syntactic slot in a fixed relative hierarchy.

cells: mi, ti, mu, jej, nám, vám, im
ma, ťa, ho, ju, nás, vás, ich, to

useCases.label: Past Auxiliary with Reflexive
useCases.example: Včera som sa vrátil neskoro domov.

useCases.label: Dative before Accusative
useCases.example: Peter mi to včera vysvetlil.

useCases.label: Full Clitic Cluster
useCases.example: Rodičia by nám ho určite kúpili.

examples.en: Včera som sa stretol s Michalom.
Prečo si mi to nepovedal skôr?
Oni by si ho radi pozreli.
Kedy ste sa im predstavili?
Brat mi ju nechcel požičať.

mistakes.note: A clitic can never stand at the absolute beginning of a sentence; it must adhere to the second position.
Within the clitic cluster, the dative pronoun (mu) must precede the accusative pronoun (to).
The reflexive particle (sa/si) must directly follow the auxiliary verb (si) before any case pronouns.

quiz.question: Yesterday I bought it. -> Včera ___ kúpil.
quiz.explanation: The auxiliary 'som' occupies position 1 and the accusative clitic 'to' occupies position 4 in the cluster.

quiz.question: Why didn't you tell me? -> Prečo ___ nepovedal?
quiz.explanation: The correct clitic sequence is auxiliary (si) + dative (mi) + accusative (to).

quiz.question: Choose the correctly ordered sentence.
quiz.explanation: The conditional particle 'by' precedes the reflexive pronoun 'si', which precedes accusative 'to'.

quiz.question: We introduced ourselves to them. -> My ___ predstavili.
quiz.explanation: The order is auxiliary (sme) + reflexive (sa) + dative pronoun (im).

tip: Remember the formula: Aux/By + Sa/Si + Dative + Accusative. Clitics never begin a sentence, so place a stressed word first.

title: Reflexive Verbs and the Contrast Between 'sa' and 'si'
subtitle: Distinguishing true reflexives, reciprocal actions, and self-benefactive dative actions
keyPoint: Use accusative 'sa' when the action directly targets the subject, and dative 'si' when the subject performs the action for or to their own benefit.

useCases.label: Direct Reflexive Action
useCases.example: Každé ráno sa sprchujem studenou vodou.

useCases.label: Possession or Benefit (Dative)
useCases.example: Kúpil si nový kabát na zimu.

useCases.label: Reciprocal Mutual Action
useCases.example: Priatelia si navzájom pomáhajú.

examples.en: Chlapec sa češe pred zrkadlom.
Dievča si češe dlhé vlasy.
Často sa smejeme na jeho vtipoch.
Musím si oddýchnuť po dlhej práci.
Peter a Lucia sa zobrali minulý rok.

mistakes.note: When a specific body part or external direct object is named, the reflexive pronoun must be dative 'si'.
'Báť sa' (to be afraid) is an inherently reflexive verb that always requires 'sa'.
Buying something for oneself is an indirect/benefactive action requiring 'si', not accusative 'sa'.

quiz.question: I brush my teeth every evening. -> Každý večer ___ zuby.
quiz.explanation: Because 'zuby' (teeth) is the direct accusative object, the self-affecting action takes dative 'si'.

quiz.question: Children, why are you laughing? -> Deti, prečo ___?
quiz.explanation: 'Smiať sa' is an inherently reflexive verb taking 'sa'.

quiz.question: He bought a new car for himself. -> Kúpil ___ nové auto.
quiz.explanation: Actions carried out for one's own advantage/ownership demand dative reflexive 'si'.

quiz.question: Tomáš and Marek help each other. -> Tomáš a Marek ___ pomáhajú.
quiz.explanation: Pomáhať takes a dative object, so the reciprocal 'each other' pronoun is dative 'si'.

tip: Ask: Is there already another direct object (accusative noun) in the clause? If yes, use 'si' (e.g., umyť si tvár). If the subject alone is the object, use 'sa' (umyť sa).

title: Verbs of Motion: Determinate vs. Indeterminate
subtitle: Navigating unidirectional, multidirectional, and prefixed motion verbs
keyPoint: Determinate verbs denote unidirectional motion happening at one specific moment, while indeterminate verbs denote repeated, round-trip, or multidirectional motion.

useCases.label: Specific Progressive Motion
useCases.example: Práve teraz idem pešo do obchodu.

useCases.label: Habitual or Round-Trip
useCases.example: Každý deň chodím do práce električkou.

useCases.label: Prefixed Perfective Departure
useCases.example: Vlak už odišiel zo stanice.

examples.en: Kam teraz ideš tak rýchlo?
Môj otec chodí každé ráno behať.
Lietadlo práve letí nad Bratislavou.
Vtáky na jeseň lietajú na juh.
Kedy konečne prídeš na návštevu?

mistakes.note: Use determinate 'ísť' for motion happening right now in one specific direction.

mistakes.wrong: Každú nedeľu idem k starým rodičom.
mistakes.right: Každú nedeľu chodím k starým rodičom.
mistakes.note: Repeated, habitual journeys require indeterminate 'chodiť'.

mistakes.wrong: Včera som išiel do kina a vrátil som sa.
mistakes.right: Včera som bol v kine. / Včera som išiel do kina...
mistakes.note: If a completed round trip is meant without emphasis on the outbound leg, Slovak prefers 'bol som' or 'chodil'.

quiz.question: Where are you going right now? -> Kam práve teraz ___?
quiz.explanation: Determinate 'ideš' expresses unidirectional movement in progress right now.

quiz.question: My son attends elementary school. -> Môj syn ___ do základnej školy.
quiz.explanation: Habitual attendance over a prolonged period requires indeterminate 'chodiť'.

quiz.question: Look, that bird is flying very low! -> Pozri, ten vták ___ veľmi nízko!
quiz.explanation: A single continuous flight observed right now calls for determinate 'letieť' (letí).

quiz.question: He has already left home. -> Už ___ z domu preč.
quiz.explanation: The prefix 'od-' marks departure/leaving, combined with ísť -> odísť (past: odišiel).

tip: Ask yourself: Is it happening right now in one line (ísť/letieť/bežať), or is it a repeat habit or wandering around (chodiť/lietať/behať)?

title: The Rhythmic Law (Rytmický zákon) and Exceptions
subtitle: Mastering Slovak vowel shortening and its systematic exceptions
keyPoint: In standard Slovak, two consecutive long syllables cannot follow each other within the same word; a following long vowel automatically shortens.

cells: Shortened suffix due to long stem syllable
Suffix remains long after short stem

useCases.label: Adjective Inflexion
useCases.example: Máme krásny a slnečný deň.

useCases.label: Verb Conjugation
useCases.example: Každý večer píšem a čítam knihy.

useCases.label: Valid Exception (páví)
useCases.example: Na lúke leží pávie pero.

examples.en: V záhrade kvitne biely kvet.
To je veľmi múdra odpoveď.
Volám sa Juraj a bývam v Trnave.
Videli sme nádherné pávie perie.
Študenti píšu dôležitý test.

mistakes.note: Because 'krás-' has a long vowel (á), the masculine ending '-ý' shortens to '-y'.
The stem syllable 'múd-' is long (ú), forcing the feminine adjectival ending '-á' to shorten to '-a'.
The first-person singular suffix '-ám' shortens to '-am' because the stem 'býv-' has a long 'ý'.

quiz.question: Select the correctly shortened feminine form of 'krásny'.
quiz.explanation: The long root 'krás-' forces the adjectival ending '-á' to shorten to '-a' -> 'krásna'.

quiz.question: Which word is a systematic EXCEPTION to the Rhythmic Law?
quiz.explanation: Animal possessive adjectives ending in '-í' (like páví, líščí, kohútí) do not shorten their endings.

quiz.question: I write letters. -> Ja ___ listy.
quiz.explanation: In 'písať', the stem vowel 'í' is long; the present ending is short '-em' (píšem).

quiz.question: White shirt -> ___ košeľa.
quiz.explanation: The diphthong 'ie' counts phonologically as a long syllable, so the ending '-á' shortens to '-a' (biela).

tip: Diphthongs (ia, ie, iu, ô) count as long syllables! Whenever a stem has á, é, í, ó, ú, ý or a diphthong, shorten the following suffix vowel.

title: Present and Past Conditional Moods
subtitle: Hypothetical scenarios and counterfactual past reflections using 'by'
keyPoint: Form the present conditional with the past -l verb plus particle 'by' and personal auxiliary clitics, and the past conditional by inserting 'bol/bola/boli'.

cells: he would come / would have come

useCases.label: Polite Request / Present Desire
useCases.example: Radi by sme si objednali obed.

useCases.label: Hypothetical Condition
useCases.example: Keby som mal viac času, cestoval by som.

useCases.label: Unreal Past Counterfactual
useCases.example: Keby si mi zavolal, bol by som ti pomohol.

examples.en: Čo by si urobil na mojom mieste?
Veľmi rád by som navštívil Vysoké Tatry.
Keby sme mali peniaze, kúpili by sme si dom.
Včera by bol prišiel, ale ochorel.
Bez teba by sme to nikdy neboli dokázali.

mistakes.note: 'Keby' already embeds the conditional marker 'by'; never add another 'by' after 'keby'.
In the 1st and 2nd persons, the auxiliary clitic ('som/si/sme/ste') is obligatory with 'by'.

mistakes.wrong: On by bol prišiel včera, keby vedel by.
mistakes.right: On by bol prišiel včera, keby bol vedel.
mistakes.note: In the 'keby' clause, use the past conditional (keby bol vedel) without adding a redundant 'by'.

quiz.question: I would like to help you. -> Rád ___ pomohol.
quiz.explanation: 1st person singular present conditional requires 'by' + 'som' along with the dative pronoun 'ti'.

quiz.question: If we had time, we would go. -> ___ čas, išli by sme.
quiz.explanation: 'Keby' already contains 'by', so you only attach the auxiliary 'sme' without duplicating 'by'.

quiz.question: She would have bought that book yesterday. -> Ona ___ tú knihu kúpila.
quiz.explanation: 3rd person feminine past conditional requires 'by bola' + past tense verb ('kúpila').

quiz.question: What would you (singular informal) say? -> Čo ___?
quiz.explanation: 2nd person singular conditional requires 'by si' followed by the masculine -l participle 'povedal'.

tip: Remember: 'Keby' already has 'by' built into it! Never say 'keby by som'; say 'keby som'.

title: Impersonal and Reflexive Passive Constructions
subtitle: Use 3rd person verbs with 'sa' to express general truths, states, and agentless actions
keyPoint: Combine the reflexive particle 'sa' with a 3rd person singular verb to describe general statements or actions where the agent is omitted.

cells: Nominative plural object + 3rd person pl. + sa

useCases.label: Rules and Prohibitions
useCases.example: V knižnici sa nehovorí nahlas.

useCases.label: Subjective Well-being / States
useCases.example: V novom byte sa nám býva príjemne.

useCases.label: Product or Process Descriptions
useCases.example: Tento liek sa užíva ráno.

examples.en: V našej obci sa stavia nová škola.
Ako sa píše toto slovo?
V nedeľu sa tu nepracuje.
Na Slovensku sa pije veľa minerálnej vody.
Pri mori sa mi dýchalo veľmi ľahko.

mistakes.wrong: Ľudia hovoria sa, že bude zima.
mistakes.note: Do not include an explicit agent like 'ľudia' when using the impersonal reflexive 'hovorí sa'.

mistakes.wrong: Tu nie je dovolené fajčiť sa.
mistakes.note: To state a general ban concisely, attach 'sa' directly to the verb 'fajčiť' instead of calquing from English.
Impersonal state expressions take the experiencer in the dative case (mi), never the nominative (ja).

quiz.question: How do you say 'How is this dish prepared?'
quiz.explanation: The 3rd person singular with reflexive 'sa' forms the passive: 'Ako sa pripravuje...'

quiz.question: Complete the prohibition: 'V múzeu ___ (no taking photos).'
quiz.explanation: General bans use the impersonal 3rd person singular form with 'sa': 'sa nefotografuje'.

quiz.question: Which sentence correctly expresses 'I study well here'?
quiz.explanation: Experiencer states require the dative pronoun 'mi' alongside the impersonal reflexive verb.

quiz.question: Choose the correct reflexive passive: 'New cars are sold here.'
quiz.explanation: Because 'nové autá' is plural nominative, the verb agrees in the plural: 'sa predávajú'.

tip: Think of 3rd person + 'sa' as the Slovak equivalent of English 'one does' or 'people do'; it avoids passive participles in everyday speech.

title: Relative Clauses and Declension of 'ktorý'
subtitle: Connect ideas by choosing the proper gender, number, and case for 'which' and 'who'
keyPoint: The pronoun 'ktorý' takes its gender and number from the noun it modifies, but its grammatical case depends entirely on its role inside the relative clause.

useCases.label: Subject of Relative Clause
useCases.example: Poznám muža, ktorý hovorí piatimi jazykmi.

useCases.label: Direct Object of Relative Clause
useCases.example: To je tá kniha, ktorú som hľadal.

useCases.label: Prepositional Complement
useCases.example: Mesto, v ktorom žijem, je veľmi tiché.

examples.en: Hľadám dievča, ktoré stratilo tento batoh.
Auto, ktoré sme kúpili minulý týždeň, je úsporné.
Študenti, ktorým profesor pomohol, zložili skúšku.
Vidíš ten dom, pred ktorým stojí policajné auto?
Lekárka, o ktorej sme sa rozprávali, pracuje v nemocnici.

mistakes.wrong: Žena, čo vidím, je moja teta.
mistakes.right: Žena, ktorú vidím, je moja teta.
mistakes.note: While 'čo' is common in casual spoken Slovak, standard grammar requires 'ktorú' (feminine accusative).

mistakes.wrong: To sú muži, ktoré nám pomohli.
mistakes.right: To sú muži, ktorí nám pomohli.
mistakes.note: Masculine animate nominative plural requires 'ktorí' with a soft 'í', not 'ktoré'.

mistakes.wrong: Kniha som kúpil včera je dobrá.
mistakes.right: Kniha, ktorú som kúpil včera, je dobrá.
mistakes.note: Unlike English, Slovak never omits the relative pronoun and always requires a separating comma.

quiz.question: Identify the right form: 'Kaviareň, do ___ často chodíme, je dnes zatvorená.'
quiz.explanation: The preposition 'do' requires the genitive case. 'Kaviareň' is feminine, so 'do ktorej' is correct.

quiz.question: Fill the blank: 'To sú priatelia, ___ som pozval na večeru.'
quiz.explanation: The relative pronoun is the direct object (accusative plural animate) of 'pozval', so 'ktorých' is required.

quiz.question: Choose the right relative pronoun: 'Mám nové auto, ___ má výborný motor.'
quiz.explanation: 'Auto' is neuter singular and serves as the subject (nominative) in the subclause, yielding 'ktoré'.

quiz.question: Pick the correct form: 'Učiteľ, s ___ sme hovorili, bol milý.'
quiz.explanation: The preposition 's' (with) governs the instrumental case: masculine singular instrumental is 's ktorým'.

tip: Always write a comma before 'ktorý', and remember that English allows omitting 'which' or 'that', but Slovak never drops the relative pronoun.

title: Active and Passive Adjectival Participles
subtitle: Form and decline '-úci/-iaci' and '-ný/-tý' verbal adjectives for formal writing
keyPoint: Present active participles end in '-úci/-iaci' and express ongoing action by an agent, while passive participles end in '-ný/-tý' and describe the recipient of a completed or ongoing action.

useCases.label: Active Ongoing Modifier
useCases.example: Vlak vezúci stovky cestujúcich meškal.

useCases.label: Passive State Modifier
useCases.example: Všetky predložené dokumenty boli schválené.

useCases.label: Compound Analytical Passive
useCases.example: Tento most bol postavený v minulom storočí.

examples.en: Na ulici sme videli spievajúce deti.
Dvere na kancelárii zostali zatvorené celý deň.
Zákazníci čakajúci v rade boli netrpezliví.
Balík odoslaný včera dorazí až v pondelok.
Tento článok bol napísaný skúseným novinárom.

mistakes.note: When modifying a noun ('človeka' in acc. sg.), the active participle must decline like an adjective ('píšuceho'), not stay uninflected.
Use the passive participle ending '-ná' with 'byť' for passive constructions, never the past tense '-la'.
Verbs like 'umyť' take the suffix '-tý' (yielding 'umytý/umytá/umyté'), not '-ený'.

quiz.question: Select the correct present active participle: 'Muž ___ kávu číta noviny.'
quiz.explanation: 'Muž' is masculine nominative singular, requiring the nominative adjective form 'pijúci'.

quiz.question: Select the correct passive form: 'Všetky úlohy boli úspešne ___.'
quiz.explanation: 'Úlohy' is feminine plural nominative, so the passive participle must match in feminine/inanimate plural: 'dokončené'.

quiz.question: Which verb forms its passive participle with the suffix '-tý'?
quiz.explanation: 'Zavrieť' forms 'zavretý' (also 'zatvorený' exists from 'zatvoriť', but 'zavrieť' strictly takes '-tý').

quiz.question: Choose the right participle: 'Hovoril o študentoch ___ na univerzite.'
quiz.explanation: The preposition 'o' with 'študentoch' triggers locative plural: 'o študujúcich'.

tip: Active participles decline like 'cudzí' (soft paradigm), whereas passive participles decline like 'pekný' (hard paradigm).

title: The Transgressive (Prechodník) for Concurrent Actions
subtitle: Condense subordinate clauses using verbal adverbs ending in '-úc' or '-iac'
keyPoint: The transgressive expresses a secondary action performed simultaneously by the same subject as the main verb and never changes for gender, number, or case.

useCases.label: Simultaneous Background Action
useCases.example: Počúval hudbu, kráčajúc po tichej ulici.

useCases.label: Cause or Manner
useCases.example: Nemajúc dostatok peňazí, rozhodol sa ostať doma.

useCases.label: Literary and Formal Narration
useCases.example: Odišiel z miestnosti, nehovoriac ani slovo.

examples.en: Sedela pri okne, premýšľajúc o svojej budúcnosti.
Pozdravil nás, usmievajúc sa od ucha k uchu.
Vstúpil do izby, držiac v rukách horúci čaj.
Nevediac kam ísť, spýtal sa okoloidúceho na cestu.
Chlapci utekali domov, smejúc sa celou cestou.

mistakes.wrong: Kráčajúc po ulici, zrazu spadol dážď.
mistakes.right: Keď kráčal po ulici, zrazu začalo pršať.
mistakes.note: Dangling participle: the subject of the transgressive ('kráčajúc') must be identical to the subject of the main clause.

mistakes.right: Ona pracujúc píše správy. (Better: Pracujúc píše správy or Pri práci píše správy.)
mistakes.note: Prechodník is indeclinable: never add adjectival endings like '-úca' or '-iaca' to form an adverbial participle.
Check the 3rd person plural stem ('robia' → stem 'rob-' + '-iac' = 'robiac').

quiz.question: Form the transgressive of 'čítať' (3rd pl. 'čítajú'):
quiz.explanation: Remove '-ú' from the 3rd person plural 'čítajú' and append '-úc': 'čítajúc'.

quiz.question: Identify the sentence that correctly employs a transgressive:
options: Pozerajúc film, zjedol celú misku pukancov.
quiz.explanation: The subject doing the watching must be the one performing the main action ('on zjedol'). The others are dangling participles.

quiz.question: What is the transgressive of 'sedieť' (3rd pl. 'sedia')?
quiz.explanation: From the 3rd person plural 'sedia', add '-c' to form the verbal adverb 'sediac'.

quiz.question: Which English structure best matches the Slovak prechodník?
options: The present participle '-ing' indicating simultaneous action
The infinitive of purpose 'in order to'
quiz.explanation: Prechodník represents an action happening at the same time as the main verb, mirroring English '-ing' clauses (e.g., 'Smiling, he entered').

tip: Never decline a transgressive for gender or number: whether 'he', 'she', or 'they' is doing the action, 'krFieldáčajúc' remains unchanged.

title: Advanced Verbal Prefixation and Semantic Shifts
subtitle: Transform verb meanings and aspect using prefixes like pre-, vy-, za-, od-, and pri-
keyPoint: Prefixes in Slovak not only turn imperfective verbs into perfective ones, but they also systematically alter spatial trajectory, intensity, and lexical meaning.

useCases.label: Spatial Movement
useCases.example: Vták preletel cez záhradu a vyletel z klietky.

useCases.label: Change of State or Thoroughness
useCases.example: Študent si dôkladne prečítal celú knihu.

useCases.label: Starting an Action (Ingressive)
useCases.example: Keď zbadala psa, zrazu sa rozplakala.

examples.en: Musíš ten text prepísať, lebo je v ňom veľa chýb.
Vlak do Košíc práve odišiel zo stanice.
Kedy k nám zajtra prídete na návštevu?
Firma vyvinula úplne novú aplikáciu.
Vodič zaparkoval auto pred naším domom.

mistakes.note: 'Odcestovať' is perfective (completed action). For an ongoing action happening right now, use imperfective 'odchádzať'.
'Pri-' indicates arrival or approach toward the speaker. To move out from inside, use 'vy-' ('vyšiel som').

mistakes.right: Zabil som čas čítaním. / Prečítal som to za dve hodiny.
mistakes.note: Be careful with figurative vs. literal prefixes; 'prečítať' expresses reading completely from start to finish.

quiz.question: Which prefixed verb means 'to cross the street on foot'?
quiz.explanation: The prefix 'pre-' denotes movement across or through a barrier or space: 'prejsť cez ulicu'.

quiz.question: Choose the verb that means 'to earn money by working':
quiz.explanation: 'Zarobiť' specifically means to earn money through labor.

quiz.question: What is the meaning of 'odniesť' compared to 'priniesť'?
options: To carry inside vs. to carry outside
To carry away vs. to bring toward
To finish carrying vs. to start carrying
To carry poorly vs. to carry well
quiz.explanation: 'Od-' conveys motion away from a point, while 'pri-' indicates motion toward or bringing to a destination.

quiz.question: Which verb means 'to thoroughly examine / look through'?
quiz.explanation: 'Prehliadnuť' (si) means to inspect or look thoroughly through something (e.g., medical exam or sights).

tip: Prefixes almost always turn an imperfective verb perfective. If you need an ongoing imperfective with the new prefix meaning, look for the suffixed secondary imperfective (e.g., prečítať → prečítavať).
